title: MatUQ: a benchmark for uncertainty-aware out-of-distribution materials property prediction with graph neural networks
title_zh: MatUQ：图神经网络材料性质预测的不确定性与分布外基准
summary: MatUQ 将材料图神经网络的分布外预测与不确定性评估放在同一基准中。现有信息未披露数据集、模型、校准策略和定量结果。对团队而言，最直接的价值是为机器学习势、机器学习 Kohn-Sham 哈密顿量和缺陷性质模型建立可比较的置信度评测协议。
abstract: npj Computational Materials, Published online: 15 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41524-026-02272-x MatUQ: a benchmark for uncertainty-aware out-of-distribution materials property prediction with graph neural networks

title: A Bit of Freedom Goes a Long Way: Classical and Quantum Algorithms for Reinforcement Learning under a Generative Model
title_zh: 生成模型下强化学习的经典与量子算法
summary: 工作研究可间歇调用生成式环境模拟器的强化学习，并结合经典与量子策略近似算法。核心设定是线上交互和离线生成采样混合，而非具体材料模拟。摘要未提供样本复杂度、量子查询优势或实验任务，因此对材料主动学习的启发目前只能停留在模拟器驱动策略搜索层面。
abstract: We propose novel classical and quantum online algorithms for learning finite- and infinite-horizon Markov Decision Processes (MDPs). Our algorithms are based on a hybrid online-offline reinforcement learning model wherein the agent can, from time to time, freely interact with the environment in a generative sampling fashion, i.e., by having access to a ''simulator''. By employing known classical and new quantum algorithms for approximating optimal policies under a generative model within our learning algorithms, we show that it is possible to avoid several paradigms from RL like ''optimism in the face of uncertainty'' and ''posterior sampling'' and instead compute and use optimal policies directly, which yields better regret bounds compared to previous works. Our quantum algorithms obtain regret bounds which only a operatornamepolylogT dependence on the number of time steps T, thus breaking the O(sqrtT) classical barrier. Our infinite-horizon discounted regret bound is brand new, while in the finite- and infinite-horizon undiscounted settings, our results match the time dependence of some prior quantum works, but with improved dependence on other parameters like state space size S and action space size A.

title: Physics-informed distribution of relaxation times estimation and latent-space condition monitoring of solid oxide fuel and electrolysis cells from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy
title_zh: 物理信息弛豫时间分布估计与固体氧化物电池状态监测
summary: 作者用物理信息卷积自编码器从电化学阻抗谱直接恢复弛豫时间分布。关键约束是把阻抗—弛豫分布的离散映射写入训练损失，从而避免逐谱选择正则化。合成测试能解析重叠过程，但现有摘要没有给出固体氧化物电池真实数据上的误差、寿命预测或状态监测增益。
abstract: arXiv:2608.13305v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Estimating the distribution of relaxation times (DRT) fromelectrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is an ill-posed inverse problem that is highly sensitive to regularisation choices. We propose a physics-informed convolutional autoencoder that estimates DRT directly from EIS data without spectrum-specific tuning. A discretised relation between impedance and the DRT is embedded in the training process, constraining the network to produce impedance-consistent distributions. The model resolves overlapping relaxation processes in synthetic two-ZARC spectra and accurately reconstructs measurements from three independent solid oxide fuel and electrolysis cell datasets, with range-normalised errors below 1.1%. Decoder-probe analysis shows that the learned latent representation is organised according to relaxation timescale. Distances in this latent space capture operating changes, hydrogen-shortage events, and long-term degradation. The same lightweight architecture is applied across all datasets without modification, providing consistent DRT estimation and an interpretable basis for condition monitoring.

title: AutoQuREO: A Framework for Automated Quantum Resource Estimation and Optimization
title_zh: AutoQuREO：量子资源自动估计与优化框架
summary: AutoQuREO 面向异构量子硬件和软件栈，试图自动完成量子资源估计及优化。其问题定义超出单纯门数统计，强调编译、硬件约束和系统级代价的联动。摘要缺少算法实现、资源指标和实验数值，因此尚不能判断它对量子材料模拟、电子结构或量子动力学有何实际加速。
abstract: arXiv:2608.12936v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As quantum computing progresses from proof-of-principle demonstrations toward practical utility, a significant impediment is the need to augment algorithmic feasibility with system-level optimization across heterogeneous hardware and software stacks. Quantum resource estimation (QRE) plays a central role in this transition, yet existing approaches remain largely compilation-heavy or domain-knowledge-guided symbolic annotations, and tightly coupled to long-term fault-tolerant assumptions, limiting their topical applicability. In this work, we introduce AutoQuREO, an Automated framework for full-stack Quantum Resource Estimation and Optimization. AutoQuREO is built around four core novelties: (i) a flexible, user-defined abstraction of the quantum computing stack; (ii) a modular library of reusable stack components enabling rapid full-stack prototyping; (iii) surrogate modeling of layer-wise resources via algorithmic profiling and neuro-symbolic learning; and (iv) integrated multi-objective optimization that embeds QRE directly into deployment pipelines. Together, these design choices enable AutoQuREO to serve as a digital twin for quantum computing stacks, supporting the tractable exploration of complex design spaces. We demonstrate the capabilities of AutoQuREO through representative co-design case studies, including early-fault-tolerant quantum algorithms, small error correction codes, gate decomposition and variational training of parametric quantum circuits. These examples illustrate how AutoQuREO enables systematic discovery of unexploited resource trade-offs that are computationally intractable or abstruse using existing QRE tools. AutoQuREO is positioned as a general-purpose platform for advancing quantum technology readiness.

title: A Unified Space–Time Finite Element Solution Framework for Electromagnetic–Mechanical Coupling Problems
title_zh: 电磁—力学耦合问题的统一时空有限元求解框架
summary: 该文把空间和时间同时离散到有限元网格，并从离散变分原理求解电磁—力学耦合。核心目标是长时间瞬态计算中的能量行为和辛结构保持，而非材料电子结构。摘要没有报告具体材料、耦合方程和数值误差，因此与团队的第一性原理、分子动力学及自旋动力学只有数值方法层面的有限关联。
abstract: Electromagnetic–mechanical coupling problems are widely encountered in engineering applications. Traditional methods mostly adopt a solution paradigm that combines spatial finite element semi-discretization with temporal integration schemes. This paradigm may introduce numerical dissipation, energy drift, or fail to preserve the underlying symplectic structure during long-term transient simulations. To address these issues, this paper introduces a space–time finite element mesh and establishes a unified space–time discrete variational framework for electromagnetic–mechanical coupling problems, thereby avoiding the conventional treatment that separates spatial discretization from temporal integration. Based on the discrete variational formulation, a unified one-step recursive scheme applicable to both nondissipative and dissipative systems is constructed, enabling the displacement field and electromagnetic fields to be solved within a unified discrete framework. Through three benchmark examples—including pure electromagnetic field problems, elastodynamic problems, and sequentially coupled electromagnetic–mechanical problems—the proposed method demonstrates its capability to accurately solve different types of physical problems within a unified framework and preserve the symplectic structure of nondissipative systems. This paper provides a unified computational approach for electromagnetic 1 fields, structural dynamics, and electromagnetic–mechanical coupling problems, enabling accurate and long-term stable transient simulations.

title: Bound gravitational waves inspired by photonic systems
title_zh: 受光子系统启发的束缚引力波
summary: 这是一篇以光子系统类比束缚引力波的新闻或科普性文章。输入信息没有给出作者、模型、方程、材料体系或可检验数值。它与团队研究的交叉仅限于波动、模式束缚和光子材料类比的概念层面，不足以支持对凝聚态机制或计算方法的实质判断。
abstract: When one mentions "waves," we immediately think of a perturbation that propagates. This applies to waves on the shore, sound waves in the air or electromagnetic waves that we use to transmit information via optical fibers. The same idea of propagating perturbations applies to gravitational waves (GWs), which entered the mainstream media a decade ago after their first direct detection. These are perturbations of the elastic fabric that we are all embedded in, called spacetime.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Variational Quantum Feature Learning for Reliable High-Dimensional Classification
title_zh: 面向可靠高维分类的不确定性感知变分量子特征学习
summary: 该工作在变分量子特征学习前加入特征置信度估计和自适应加权。创新点是让输入特征的重要性随不确定性变化，而不是等权编码。摘要没有给出量子线路、训练参数、数据集或准确率，因此无法判断其相对经典分类器和普通变分量子模型的实际收益，也与材料问题没有直接实验联系。
abstract: High-dimensional classification remains challenging for hybrid quantum–classical learning because conventional variational quantum feature learning methods often assign equal importance to all input features and do not explicitly account for feature uncertainty. This paper presents Uncertainty-Aware Variational Quantum Feature Learning (UVQFL), a hybrid framework that combines adaptive feature weighting, uncertainty estimation, and variational quantum representation learning for reliable classification. The proposed framework incorporates an Adaptive Feature Confidence Module (AFCM) to estimate the contribution of individual input features before quantum encoding and an Uncertainty Estimation Module (UEM) to characterize feature reliability during the learning process. The confidence-weighted features are encoded using a variational quantum circuit and subsequently processed by an enhanced multi-layer classical classifier. Benchmark datasets, including MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and PathMNIST, are employed during data preprocessing and quantum feature generation to establish the proposed framework. The detailed experimental evaluation, performance analysis, and comparative results presented in this study are conducted on the MNIST benchmark dataset to provide a comprehensive assessment of the proposed architecture. A systematic investigation using 4-, 6-, and 8-qubit hybrid models examines the influence of quantum feature dimensionality on classification performance. The final UVQFL model achieves a best validation accuracy of 84.62%, with 84.60% precision, 84.62% recall, and an 84.59% F1-score. The results indicate that integrating adaptive feature confidence with uncertainty-aware quantum feature learning improves feature representation quality and enhances the reliability of hybrid quantum–classical classification.
